body: Works for me! Many thanks for the time spent. I hope both your head and keyboard are fine ;)

Tried the suggestions here and also [this one](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/issues/718#issuecomment-84936730).

The only thing that eventually worked to trick web pack into ignoring the jsdom require was this:
```js
const jsdom = eval("require('jsdom')");
```

issue.title: Import through webpack fails on import-lazy

repository.name: update-notifier
repository.description: Update notifications for your CLI app

issue.body:
HI,

I am trying to use this module through webpack, and I am having some deep issues with `import-lazy` package, which seems not to be webpack friendly as well.

To make it short, I found a way to fix the build issue by using the solution mentioned here ( https://github.com/webpack/webpack/issues/4596#issuecomment-304441388 ) although it seems is not enough to make my application running on top of this package.

This is an excerpt of the error I get during runtime of my application once it is bundled with WebPack:
```
/path/to/project/dist/webpack:/node_modules/update-notifier ^\.\/.*$:16
                throw new Error("Cannot find module '" + req + "'.");
^
Error: Cannot find module 'chalk'.
    at webpackContextResolve (/path/to/project/dist/webpack:/node_modules/update-notifier ^\.\/.*$:16:1)
    at webpackContext (/path/to/project/dist/webpack:/node_modules/update-notifier ^\.\/.*$:11:1)
    at lazy (/path/to/project/dist/webpack:/node_modules/import-lazy/index.js:2:1)
    at /path/to/project/dist/webpack:/node_modules/import-lazy/index.js:10:1
    at new UpdateNotifier (/path/to/project/dist/webpack:/node_modules/update-notifier/index.js:55:1)
    at module.exports.options (/path/to/project/dist/webpack:/node_modules/update-notifier/index.js:145:1)
    at Object.__webpack_exports__.default (/path/to/project/dist/webpack:/src/index.js:31:1)
    at Object.<anonymous> (/path/to/project/bin/cli.js:5:18)
    at Module._compile (module.js:570:32)
    at Object.Module._extensions..js (module.js:579:10)
```

In my opinion there are three ways to fix it:
1) Just remove `import-lazy` and make use of the normal require ( to make it webpack friendly )
2) Publish a new package with `-webpack` suffix, but this will create maintenance overhead on your side
3) Detect if the module is being bundled with webpack, and if yes, make sure of the normal require ( not sure if it will work 100% )

Any help from your side is really appreciated. Feel free to approach me if any question arise.

Thank you and best regards,
Julian
